content.user_title: Improve UI Layout and Visual Rhythm
content.value_statement: Crowded interfaces and repetitive grids make products harder to scan and trust. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through stronger spacing, hierarchy, and responsive composition.
actual_capabilities: Assesses spacing, density, visual hierarchy, rhythm, and layout structure.
Recommends consistent spacing scales instead of arbitrary padding and margin values.
Guides selection between Flexbox, CSS Grid, and named grid areas.
Identifies repetitive card grids and suggests more varied composition patterns.
Provides verification checks for hierarchy, breathing room, consistency, and responsiveness.
limitations: Requires enough UI context to judge spacing and hierarchy accurately.
Does not include visual assets, screenshots, or automated rendering checks by itself.
Depends on an external /impeccable skill for its full preparation workflow.
Design recommendations still need implementation and browser testing.

use_cases.title: Refine a Crowded Product Screen
use_cases.description: Improve spacing, grouping, and density so operational users can scan content faster.

use_cases.title: Fix Repetitive Marketing Sections
use_cases.description: Break monotonous card grids with stronger hierarchy, asymmetry, and section rhythm.

use_cases.title: Review Responsive Layout Decisions
use_cases.description: Choose Flexbox or Grid patterns that match the content and adapt across screen sizes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Spacing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a single page or component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface for spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy. Suggest the smallest layout changes that would make it easier to scan.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Card Layout Rhythm
prompt_templates.prompt: Find repetitive card grids in this UI and propose a stronger composition. Keep the design practical and responsive.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Responsive Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a layout plan for this screen. Choose Flexbox or Grid for each major area and define spacing, density, and hierarchy rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Design System Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these screens for layout consistency. Identify spacing scale issues, weak hierarchy, card overuse, and responsive risks.

output_examples.input: A dashboard feels dense, with every widget using the same card size and spacing.
output_examples.output: The review highlights weak grouping, repeated card rhythm, and unclear priority. It recommends tighter related groups, wider section gaps, and varied widget spans.

output_examples.input: A landing page has several identical icon, heading, and text card rows.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a more varied section structure with asymmetric alignment, fewer cards, clearer content hierarchy, and responsive spacing adjustments.

output_examples.input: A settings page needs better layout rules for desktop and mobile.
output_examples.output: The result compares Flexbox and Grid choices, defines spacing behavior, and adds verification checks for hierarchy and responsiveness.

best_practices: Provide screenshots, component code, or clear screen descriptions before asking for layout changes.
Ask for a spacing scale and hierarchy plan before requesting implementation edits.
Verify final changes across mobile and desktop viewports.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for generic polish without showing the screen or describing the layout problem.
Do not apply equal spacing everywhere just to make values consistent.
Do not convert every section into cards when spacing and dividers would be clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill improve?
faq.answer: It improves layout structure, spacing, density, visual hierarchy, rhythm, and responsive composition.

faq.question: Can it edit frontend code?
faq.answer: It can guide code edits when the host tool has file access and the relevant UI code is available.

faq.question: Does it require screenshots?
faq.answer: Screenshots are not required, but they make layout assessment more accurate.

faq.question: How does it choose Flexbox or Grid?
faq.answer: It recommends Flexbox for one-dimensional layouts and Grid for two-dimensional page structures.

faq.question: Is this only for marketing pages?
faq.answer: No. It also applies to dashboards, product screens, settings pages, and design system layouts.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the screen goal, target users, current layout issue, and any relevant screenshots or component code.
